title: Operator-guided intake for batching, quantization, and routing optimization requests
creator: Aisha Bhandari
description: Create an operator-guided intake and prioritization playbook for customer requests focused on batching/caching knobs, quantization profile recommendations, and routing policy changes. Goal: reduce time-to-resolution for enterprise advisory requests, surface measurable trade-offs (latency vs cost vs quality), and ensure predictable handoffs to engineering/concierge teams.
background: We receive a steady stream of optimization requests that vary from trivial knob tweaks to multistage quantization pilots requiring infra changes. Current intake is inconsistent: some customers use support tickets, others email solutions, and engineering gets ad-hoc requests that bypass prioritization. This causes long lead times, unclear SLAs, and quality regressions. We need a structured, operator-driven intake to classify, score, and route requests to the appropriate lane (self-serve docs, concierge, dedicated optimization, or engineering project).
scoring_rubric: Weighting: SLA sensitivity 30%, expected cost delta 25%, traffic volume 20%, regression risk 15%, strategic value 10%
SLA sensitivity: measured by percentile latency SLO impact and user-facing error tolerance
Expected cost delta: estimate in $/1M tokens after recommended change
Traffic volume: current qps and peak tokens/minute; higher weight for high-volume customers
Regression risk: model/quality impact likelihood (low/medium/high) based on test prompt set
Strategic value: partnership level, logo, or referenceability
triage_lanes: Self-serve: documentation + recommended knob recipes for common patterns (auto-batching, TTL cache, default quant profiles). Fastest to close.
Concierge (Operator-led): runbench, suggestion of knob changes, quantify cost/latency impacts; 2-week advisory engagement.
Engineering-led: changes that require runtime/kernel work, new quant profile support, or routing infra changes; handled as scoped ENG work after intake.
Escalation to Customer Success/Account team for contract/SLA negotiations and manual rolling policies.
Compliance path: requests involving private deployment/KMS or audit logs routed to Security & Compliance review.
intake_fields: Primary contact and desired SLA/latency targets
Workload characteristics: average tokens/req, request distribution, sequence length percentiles
Current model & variant, token cost baseline, p50/p95/p99 latency, failure modes
Prompts/representative input set (required for quality checks)
Business impact estimate and desired timeline
decision_points: If score >= 80: automatic routing to Concierge lane with 48h initial response and a 2-week advisory window
If score 50-79: recommend self-serve plan + optional concierge pilot at cost; engineering involvement only if pilot shows regression or infra blockers
If score < 50: respond with self-serve resources and request re-submission with more telemetry
Any request touching private/on-prem KMS or requiring new audit controls triggers Security review and Engineering hold
operator_playbook_steps: 1) Validate form fields and reproduce baseline metrics via instrumentation dashboard link
2) Run automated lightweight microbench (cost/latency estimate) on a staging mirror where possible
3) Apply candidate knob delta(s) in a sandbox using standardized recipes (batch_size, padding policy, kv_cache TTL, quant profile), capture before/after metrics
4) Run representative prompt set for quality regression check (automatic diff + human sample check for top-10 prompts), document output delta
5) Produce advisory note with recommended change, expected savings, latency delta, regression risk and rollout recommendations
6) Route to the appropriate lane with explicit acceptance criteria and rollback plan
sample_knob_recipes: Batching: dynamic_batch_size with cap of 32 for short sequences and 8 for long sequences; prefer greedy batching window 20ms for interactive workloads
Caching: prefix-based KV cache with 24h TTL for sessioned chat; heuristics to avoid caching prompts with high personalization tokens
Quantization: baseline 8-bit int8 for non-sensitive models; 4-bit (QLoRA-style) for cost-critical LLMs after quality guardrails
Routing policy: latency-first route to regional low-latency pool, cost-first route to quantized variant with degrade-to-low-cost-fallback
acceptance_criteria: Intake form and scoring service implemented and validated with 3 pilot customers
Operator checklist and sandbox runbook published in Confluence
Console: ability to flag requests and route to Concierge or Engineering with SLA tags
Observed reduction in average time-to-first-response from 5 business days to <=48 hours for high-score requests
One recorded pilot showing >=20% cost savings without >5% quality regression on monitored prompt set

risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Quality regressions from aggressive quantization — Mitigation: gated pilots with prompt-set guards and mandatory human review for top-10 prompts
Risk: Overloading Concierge capacity — Mitigation: soft quota and SLA gating; automations to fallback to self-serve when load > threshold
Risk: Security/compliance delays for Private customers — Mitigation: pre-defined compliance checklist and early Security involvement in intake
Risk: Insufficient telemetry to score requests — Mitigation: intake requires minimum telemetry fields; otherwise classify as low-confidence and request more data
